local_path_policy: The upstream repository was cloned into a temporary /tmp checkout for inspection, but the temp filesystem path is intentionally omitted from this ledger shard because it is local machine state and not product design state.
inspection_commands: rg -n quota/favorites/priority/router/schema/sync/probe/update/docker patterns in README.md and src/core/**

sed/nl inspection of src/core/quota-capabilities.js, src/core/provider-quota-fetchers.js, src/core/router-daemon.js, src/core/sync-set.js, src/core/token-usage-reader.js, src/core/favorites.js, and related TUI/help files
quota_and_usage_notes: Upstream distinguishes quota telemetry capabilities by provider, including `header`, `endpoint`, and `unknown` signal types, plus display modes such as `percent` and `ok` and reset cadences such as rolling, daily, monthly, none, and unknown.
Provider quota fetchers currently include endpoint polling for OpenRouter and SiliconFlow-style user-info parsing, with TTL caching, error backoff, and pending-request coalescing.

Upstream runtime also infers quota/rate-limit exhaustion from HTTP 429, quota/rate-limit text, retry headers, and provider response metadata. PM should map those into Usage pressure/cooldown evidence instead of copying upstream state stores.

Upstream token usage reader reads provider/model quota snapshots from its own token stats JSON. PM should not reuse the upstream file path or persistence shape directly; it should map the useful concepts into PM storage and Usage projections.
routing_and_priority_notes: Upstream router sets use explicit priority order for selected models. The current router sorts by explicit priority first, then circuit state, then score, with the health score used as a tie-breaker rather than letting a low-priority faster model steal traffic.

Upstream favorites preserve insertion/order priority and support reorder up/down. TUI/help text describes router fallback order and a favorites-oriented fallback chain; PM's requested top-10 priority setting should adapt the concept natively.

Upstream circuit breaker state tracks CLOSED, HALF_OPEN, OPEN-like conditions, auth errors, stale/unsupported flags, cooldowns, consecutive failures, quota_exhausted, and quota details. PM should map these to existing health, availability, pressure, cooldown, and resolution-outcome concepts.
probe_sync_update_notes: Upstream `sync-set` builds a router set from active routeable providers with API keys, ranks candidates, live-probes response and tool-call behavior, writes the best set, and signals daemon reload.
Upstream probing is useful source behavior but can spend free quota. PM needs native policy controls for probe cadence, confidence, cancellation, and quota cost.
Upstream web/server exposes router set management, reorder, sync, probe-all, and update behavior. PM should adapt concepts, not expose or depend on those endpoints as-is.
native_integration_notes: Upstream supports Docker and a local daemon/web dashboard, but Jared explicitly said PM likely should not run it as Docker because the PM integration should be native.

PM should not inherit upstream telemetry, local config path, credential storage, external endpoint installer, daemon port, or self-update behavior without PM-owned security, storage, permissions, and FileSafe design.
pm_design_implications: Free Models should reuse PM's Usage-owned pressure/cooldown/switch semantics from Multi-Account where possible.
The user's top-10 priority list should be authoritative among eligible models, with pressure/health/cooldown filtering and PM scoring as secondary signals.
Every Free Models row should preserve hidden upstream_provider, provider/model identity, quota signal confidence, source version/tag/SHA, and import disposition.

Every active upstream free/free-limited model can be shown under one PM provider if the GUI uses badges to make setup, quota, rate-limit, account, billing/free-limited, and confidence distinctions explicit.
